quirks.description: Strapi supports multiple upload providers (local, AWS S3, Cloudinary, DigitalOcean Spaces, MinIO). URL base changes per provider but the filename hash suffix (_[10-hex-chars]) is preserved across all.
quirks.workaround: Match the _[0-9a-f]{10} suffix pattern regardless of domain/path. This is the definitive Strapi fingerprint from crypto.randomBytes(5).toString('hex').

quirks.description: Strapi generates responsive formats as filename prefixes. v4: thumbnail_, small_, medium_, large_. v5 adds: xsmall_ (64px), xlarge_ (1920px).
quirks.workaround: Strip prefix (thumbnail_|xsmall_|small_|medium_|large_|xlarge_) to find original filename.

quirks.description: When using Cloudinary provider, transforms use path syntax (e.g., /c_fill,w_800,h_600/ and /q_auto,f_auto/).
quirks.workaround: Detect Cloudinary URLs and strip transform segments from path to get original. Re-apply via Cloudinary URL builder.

quirks.description: Strapi is headless with NO client-side JS markers. Detection relies entirely on image URL patterns. If frontend proxies images (e.g., Next.js Image /_next/image?url=...), Strapi becomes undetectable.
quirks.workaround: This is a fundamental limitation. The 10-char hex suffix in filenames is the only reliable signal.

quirks.description: Many Strapi sites serve the API from a subdomain (e.g., api.example.com/uploads/). Images have a different origin than the page.
quirks.workaround: urlPatterns match against full page HTML source, catching cross-origin image URLs.

quirks.description: Strapi v3 uses pure 32-char MD5 hash filenames (113a96e0c7a0475ea85aa919c7097717.jpg) without the name_hash structure. These will NOT be detected by current patterns.
quirks.workaround: Known limitation. v3 sites are increasingly rare. Manual adapter configuration may be needed.
